Logarithmic L2 isometry gives kernel q_b, Fourier multiplier B(1/2+iτ,b+1/2−iτ). Outside its completed range a full-line inverse compressed to the half-line is a Fredholm parametrix modulo Hilbert--Schmidt cross terms; on every curve point escaping unit packets form a weakly-null approximate eigenfamily. Zero follows by closedness. Digamma monotonicity makes the curve nonreal for every b>0. No numerical experiment substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: The Fredholm essential spectrum is a natural invariant needed to understand solvability and perturbation stability of the exact b-parameter Hardy operator introduced in the 2026 primary source. The explicit gamma-beta curve reveals a qualitative transition from the real essential spectrum of the classical Hilbert matrix to nonreal essential spectral points for every b>0. Obtaining both directions requires compact reductions and non-Fredholm singular sequences; this is not a renormalization or a routine norm bound.
